<summary>📝 Walkthrough</summary>

## Walkthrough

A helper function `platformHasCloudNetworkConfigController` was added to return true for AWS, Azure, GCP, and OpenStack. `checkOperandsRolloutStatus` was modified to include the `cloud-network-config-controller` operand in rollout readiness checks only when the hosted control plane platform type matches those platforms; otherwise it is not appended. The prior unconditional inclusion of `cloud-network-config-controller` from the OVNKubernetes-specific operand list was removed. A unit test `TestPlatformHasCloudNetworkConfigController` was added to validate the helper across platform types.

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/hypershift/pull/8238): >## What this PR does / why we need it: > >The `checkOperandsRolloutStatus` function in the CNO ControlPlaneComponent unconditionally expects the `cloud-network-config-controller` deployment to exist when `NetworkType` is `OVNKubernetes`. This causes the CNO ControlPlaneComponent's `RolloutComplete` condition to be permanently `False` with reason `WaitingForOperands`: > >``` >status: > conditions: > - type: RolloutComplete > status: "False" > reason: WaitingForOperands > message: 'failed to get deployment cloud-network-config-controller: > Deployment.apps "cloud-network-config-controller" not found' >``` > >This blocks `controlPlaneVersion` from reaching `Completed`, causing all e2e tests to time out on KubeVirt (and potentially other non-cloud platforms). > >This PR adds a platform check so `cloud-network-config-controller` is only expected on platforms that actually deploy it (AWS, Azure, GCP, OpenStack). > >## Which issue(s) this PR fixes: > >Fixes KubeVirt e2e test failures caused by `controlPlaneVersion` stuck at `Partial` — see [openshift/cluster-api-provider-kubevirt#415](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-api-provider-kubevirt/pull/415) and [prow job](https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test-platform-results/pr-logs/pull/openshift_cluster-api-provider-kubevirt/415/pull-ci-openshift-cluster-api-provider-kubevirt-main-e2e-hypershift-kubevirt/2042132391526404096). > >## Special notes for your reviewer: > >The bug was introduced in 59c5143166 ("feat: monitor operands rollout status for cno, storage and snapshotcontroller"). >## What this PR does / why we need it:
>
>The `checkOperandsRolloutStatus` function in the CNO ControlPlaneComponent unconditionally expects the `cloud-network-config-controller` deployment to exist when `NetworkType` is `OVNKubernetes`. However, this deployment is only created by CNO on cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP, OpenStack) that have cloud APIs for network management.
>
>On non-cloud platforms like **KubeVirt**, Agent, None, IBMCloud, and PowerVS, CNO never creates this deployment. This causes the CNO ControlPlaneComponent's `RolloutComplete` condition to be permanently `False` with reason `WaitingForOperands`:
>
>```
>status:
>  conditions:
>  - type: RolloutComplete
>    status: "False"
>    reason: WaitingForOperands
>    message: 'failed to get deployment cloud-network-config-controller:
>              Deployment.apps "cloud-network-config-controller" not found'
>```
>
>This blocks `controlPlaneVersion` from reaching `Completed`, causing all e2e tests to time out on KubeVirt (and potentially other non-cloud platforms).
>
>This PR adds a platform check so `cloud-network-config-controller` is only expected on platforms that actually deploy it (AWS, Azure, GCP, OpenStack).
>
>## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
>
>Fixes KubeVirt e2e test failures caused by `controlPlaneVersion` stuck at `Partial` — see [openshift/cluster-api-provider-kubevirt#415](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-api-provider-kubevirt/pull/415) and [prow job](https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test-platform-results/pr-logs/pull/openshift_cluster-api-provider-kubevirt/415/pull-ci-openshift-cluster-api-provider-kubevirt-main-e2e-hypershift-kubevirt/2042132391526404096).
>
>## Special notes for your reviewer:
>
>The bug was introduced in 59c5143166 ("feat: monitor operands rollout status for cno, storage and snapshotcontroller"). A later fix (1f4b7c931b) addressed the `NetworkType == Other` case but missed the platform dimension.
>
>The `cloud-network-config-controller` manages cloud-specific network configurations (e.g. EgressIP association/disassociation via cloud APIs). Platforms without cloud APIs simply don't have this deployment — CNO itself decides not to create it based on the infrastructure platform type.
>

reviews.body:
Good fix — the platform list is correct and matches where CNO actually deploys the cloud-network-config-controller (and where HyperShift provisions CNCC credentials).

One observation outside this PR's scope: in `test/e2e/v2/internal/workload_registry.go`, the `cloud-network-config-controller` workload is registered (line 103-109) without a `Platform` filter, unlike other platform-specific workloads like `cloud-credential-operator` (which has `Platform: &awsPlatform`). The v2 e2e test framework doesn't filter it by platform as a result. Currently mitigated by tests skipping when no pods are found, but it could be tightened up in a follow-up — the `WorkloadSpec` would need to support a list of platforms rather than a single one, since CNCC applies to AWS, Azure, GCP, and OpenStack.
